GEO promotion for enterprise software developers

Enterprise software is selected against business processes, existing infrastructure and implementation constraints. I test whether AI recommends a vendor in those contexts and what verifiable information is missing.

  • Role-specific questions about features, integration and scale
  • Checks of documentation, constraints and approved project references

Personally led by Alexey Yakovlev, GEO/AEO consultant

Selection barriers

Why a generic software-development pitch is insufficient

Procurement, CIOs and business owners evaluate different aspects of a solution. AI needs a precise description of what the company actually delivers.

01

Product and bespoke development are conflated

A packaged platform, customisation and a bespoke system differ in ownership, implementation risk and support. Each business model deserves a separate explanation.

02

Integration claims omit conditions

A promise to integrate with every ERP needs verified APIs, deployment models, version compatibility and responsibility boundaries.

03

Quality is described only as a slogan

Reliability, security and maintainability should be supported by design, testing practices, requirements and documented evidence rather than adjectives.

Verifiable facts

Evidence behind a credible recommendation

I verify the actual software or service, technical documents and permitted project examples. ISO/IEC 25010 outlines product quality characteristics; NIST SSDF covers secure-development practices. Neither is evidence of a vendor's compliance on its own.

  • Capabilities: product modules, target workflows, integrations, limitations and documentation
  • Quality: testing, performance, availability, maintainability, security and evidence of actual practices
  • Engagement: licensing versus bespoke work, milestones, IP terms, support and acceptance criteria

GAEO's technical B2B methodology informs the audit. Work performed for MethodLab is not presented as an enterprise software GEO case.

Scope of work

How I plan an enterprise-software GEO programme

Start with product segments and decision-maker intents, verify factual claims, then build and measure the evidence needed for recommendations.

  1. 01

    Buyer-intent baseline

    Build a query matrix for CIOs, procurement teams and functional managers by task, technology and integration scope.

  2. 02

    Document the actual offer

    Check API documents, product features, reference permissions, deployment requirements and security statements.

  3. 03

    Improve product information

    Specify service pages, integration documents, deployment guides, FAQs and relevant expert publications.

  4. 04

    Measure comparable answers

    Re-run fixed prompts and review recommendation accuracy and citations as well as BMR.

FAQ

Questions about the service

Can a software vendor without public case studies use GEO?+

Yes, with accurate technical documentation, product demonstrations and documented limitations. Do not invent clients or implementation results.

Must private API documentation be published?+

No. Publish supported integration types and requirements where permitted, while keeping sensitive internal details protected.

Does referencing ISO/IEC 25010 prove certification?+

No. It is a product-quality model, not proof that a particular vendor has passed certification or testing. All compliance claims need their own evidence.

How is non-brand software visibility measured?+

The matrix covers use cases, technologies and buyer roles without the vendor name; brand-related prompts are monitored separately.

How much does enterprise software GEO cost?+

GAEO's standard audit and monthly offers apply. Pricing scope depends on products, languages, integrations and query coverage.
